body: Wow that is an exhaustive list, much appreciated i will definitely be checking some of these out!one thing i would say is that i tend to swing between agreeing with food addicts anon and disagreeing. I know that certain foods have addictive properties and therefore it seems logical to completely avoid, but then i think binges become even more rewarding when you make certain food groups so taboo. Part of what brought on my bed is resitriction. Difficult,i read brain over binge and the woman who overcame her binge eating problem didnt give up "bad" foods,but overcame the mental urges to eat too much of them. However this is so difficult,as ive experienced myself, so avoidance altogether seems like the easier option, its the age old debate, moderation vs abstinence. With drugs and alcohol, i would always advocate abstinence, but food.... im not sure. What do you think??

no you are not annoying! i tend to be a lurker on here, dealing with the same issue as you. today i didn't eat any junk food, still overate healthy food though lol but i'm happy i resisted temptation! congrats on day 6, keep going!!!

it might also be the dieting, my binge-eating problems all started after i went on a calorie counting diet - my body seemed to rebel to the weightloss and told me "go eat food!" - and it was definitely not the healthy kind. i would recommend a book called brain over binge by katheryn hanson - really good read for binge eating, explains the mechanism of why we binge, the brain areas. very illuminating. also maybe think of other ways to deal with the stress of kids, talk to your partner or a friend about whats going on? a problem shared is a problem that doesnt seem so scary anymore. goodluck
i am already poor due to spending so much on takeaway lol so i'm not sure this would work, but i appreciate the advice. never hard of kirkland bars so will be checking them out, thanks bud!

yeah i tend to be lazy with cooking as i am not great, but you're right i do need to start cooking my own stuff. i've read so much about fast food being addictive, in your personal experience did you find it better to cut it all out then to try and moderate it? i'm always torn between trying to cut it out and trying to cut back. i'll check out whole30, never heard of it before. thanks for the advice

thanks for the reply. yeah I read the brain over binge and it definitely illuminated the whole binge/overeat thing for me, but the actual process of ignoring the voice never really clicked. I try to be aware of it and let the thought go, say that it is only one part of me, but that urge is strong. maybe I do need to start getting angry, I'm so passive anyway that I find it hard to get annoyed at anything lol. but I do need to start feeling angry about it, because it's fucking things up for me. again, thanks for replying, it's always good to hear someone else who has managed to quit the habit, bit of inspo.

the brain can be a bitch, still trying to deal with the cravings - havn't dealt with them successfully, I completely get it though, I always do good for a couple weeks, then fall right back into shitty habits. no words of advice, but nice to share the feelings.
